Successful iterations will be scaled up and integrated into the structured sorbent filte and tested in Susteon’s 1kg/day bench-scale system. Real-world performance data on the combined sorbent and filter design will drive further refinement and establish optimal operating conditions for the next scale of demonstration (15 kg/day). In concert with these efforts, Susteon will proactively engage with commercial partners and potential customers to assess the feasibility of scaling this DAC technology and derisk technical and commercial risks with the ultimate goal of deploying a 1TPD system. Market research and commercialization efforts undertaken during this project revealed several niche applications for this technology that could serve markets outside the carbon dioxide removal industry. The project team identified alternative modes of operation that yielded a low-purity stream of product gas (i.e., up to 20% CO ) that would be suited to a variety of process integrations, such as carbon mineralization and 2 artificial CO enrichment of greenhouses. In operating for low-purity CO production, the system would no 2 2 longer require energy intensive process units, such as vacuum pumps, or expensive mechanical designs for sealing the DAC modules under vacuum for achieving high purity. This configuration offers niche pathways to market entry that can complement ongoing material and process development efforts. The sorbent optimization work involved synthetic modification of the amine sites and added promoters to achieve high CO working 2 capacity and cyclic oxidative stability. The optimized sorbent, named ECCOsorb-T1, was integrated with an electrically conductive nonwoven filter substrate as the structured sorbent assembly. A commercial partner demonstrated the feasibility of manufacturing the structured sorbent filters using existing filter manufacturing infrastructure, reducing the risk and cost of further scale-up of the technology. The manufactured structured sorbent filters were tested in various configurations to establish optimal operating conditions and identify areas of improvement. Key achievements of this project include: • Development of ECCOsorb-T1, a high capacity, stable DAC sorbent that uses mild regeneration temperature (70°C) and can achieve >5 wt% CO capture in less than 30 minutes 2 •
